html:
Stefan Nemanja was the grand prince of Serbia from about 1166 to 1196 and founder of the Nemanjić dynasty, which ruled Serbia for two centuries. His seat was at Ras, near today's Novi Pazar.

He united the Serbian lands, took the coastal state of Duklja and won independence from the Byzantine Empire after the death of Manuel I. He fought heresy and built monasteries, above all Studenica. In 1196 he gave up the throne to his son Stefan, became a monk named Simeon and joined his youngest son Sava on Mount Athos, where they founded the Serbian monastery of Hilandar. He died there and was made a saint. His line built the state that later reached its peak under Dušan.
